knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/problem:
Using the fact that

$$
\frac{23\pi}{12}=\frac{7\pi}{6}+\frac{3\pi}{4},
$$

calculate the **exact** value of $\cos\left(\frac{23\pi}{12}\right)$.

$\cos\left(\frac{23\pi}{12}\right)=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x+y)=\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y.
$$

Apply it to the decomposition:

$$
\cos\left(\frac{23\pi}{12}\right)=\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{6}+\frac{3\pi}{4}\right).
$$

$$
\cos\left(\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{7\pi}{6}\right)\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)
$$

Substitute the signed special-angle values and combine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\cdot \left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\
&=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}-\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\right) \\
&=\frac{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/problem:
Using the fact that

$$
-\frac{7\pi}{12}=\frac{3\pi}{4}-\frac{4\pi}{3},
$$

calculate the **exact** value of $\cos\left(-\frac{7\pi}{12}\right)$.

$\cos\left(-\frac{7\pi}{12}\right)=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x-y)=\cos x\cos y+\sin x\sin y.
$$

Apply it to the decomposition:

$$
\cos\left(-\frac{7\pi}{12}\right)=\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}-\frac{4\pi}{3}\right).
$$

$$
\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)\cos\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)+\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)
$$

Substitute the signed special-angle values and combine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)\cdot \left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \\
&=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}+\left(- \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}\right) \\
&=\frac{- \sqrt{6} + \sqrt{2}}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:

$$
255^\circ=30^\circ+225^\circ,
$$

calculate the **exact** value of $\cos\left(255^\circ\right)$.

$\cos\left(255^\circ\right)=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x+y)=\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y.

Apply it to the decomposition:

$$
\cos\left(255^\circ\right)=\cos\left(30^\circ+225^\circ\right).
$$

$$
\cos\left(30^\circ\right)\cos\left(225^\circ\right)-\sin\left(30^\circ\right)\sin\left(225^\circ\right)

$$
\begin{aligned}

&=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}\right)-\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\right) \\

question.:question/problem:
Using the fact that

$$
165^\circ=300^\circ-135^\circ,
$$

calculate the **exact** value of $\cos\left(165^\circ\right)$.

$\cos\left(165^\circ\right)=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x-y)=\cos x\cos y+\sin x\sin y.
$$

Apply it to the decomposition:

$$
\cos\left(165^\circ\right)=\cos\left(300^\circ-135^\circ\right).
$$

$$
\cos\left(300^\circ\right)\cos\left(135^\circ\right)+\sin\left(300^\circ\right)\sin\left(135^\circ\right)
$$

Substitute the signed special-angle values and combine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\
&=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\right)+\left(- \frac{\sqrt{6}}{4}\right) \\
&=- \frac{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{11\pi}{12}=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{2\pi}{3},
$$

calculate the **exact** value of $\cos\left(\frac{11\pi}{12}\right)$.

$\cos\left(\frac{11\pi}{12}\right)=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x+y)=\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y.
$$

Apply it to the decomposition:

$$
\cos\left(\frac{11\pi}{12}\right)=\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{2\pi}{3}\right).
$$

$$
\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)-\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)
$$

Substitute the signed special-angle values and combine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\
&=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\right)-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{4} \\
&=- \frac{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}}{4}.

$$
